faqs.q: How much does a Broholmer cost to buy?
faqs.a: Reputable breeders typically charge $1,200–$4,000 for a Broholmer puppy. Prices vary by breeder reputation, health testing, and lineage. Rescue adoption fees are typically $100–$500 and include vaccinations, neutering, and microchipping.

faqs.q: What is the monthly cost of owning a Broholmer?
faqs.a: Budget $200–$400 per month for a Broholmer, covering food, preventive vet care, insurance, grooming and supplies. Large breeds cost more across every category — food portions, medication doses and professional services all scale with weight.

faqs.q: What are the biggest ongoing costs for a Broholmer?
faqs.a: The three largest annual expenses are food ($800–1,200), veterinary care ($400–$1,200 budgeted annually), and pet insurance ($800–1,800 per year). Grooming costs are lower for short-coated breeds managed at home.

faqs.q: How much does a Broholmer cost in the first year?
faqs.a: Year one costs for a Broholmer are significantly higher than subsequent years, typically $2,500–$5,000. This covers the purchase price or adoption fee, initial vet checks, vaccinations, spay/neuter, microchipping, crate, bedding, collar, leads and puppy training classes.

faqs.q: How often should I groom a Broholmer?
faqs.a: Broholmers need brushing once or twice per week.  Nails should be trimmed every 3–4 weeks. Ears should be checked and cleaned monthly.

faqs.q: Do Broholmers shed a lot?
faqs.a: Broholmers have seasonal shedding — manageable with a consistent brushing routine.

faqs.q: What grooming tools does a Broholmer need?
faqs.a: A rubber grooming glove or soft-bristle brush is sufficient for weekly maintenance on the Broholmer's short coat. Add a nail grinder and ear cleaner for a complete grooming kit.

faqs.q: How often should I bathe a Broholmer?
faqs.a: Every 4–6 weeks is appropriate for most Broholmers that live indoors. More frequent bathing is needed if they swim or spend time in mud. Over-bathing strips natural skin oils — use a pH-balanced dog shampoo rather than human products.

faqs.q: Are Broholmers easy to train?
faqs.a: Broholmers are considered easier to train than average — they respond quickly to reward-based methods and generalise cues well. Short 10–15 minute sessions outperform long correction-heavy drills.

faqs.q: What training method works best for a Broholmer?
faqs.a: Reward-based training using treats, praise and toy rewards is the most effective and well-researched approach for Broholmers. Keep sessions short and positive, end on a success, and vary your rewards to maintain engagement.

faqs.q: At what age should I start training my Broholmer?
faqs.a: Start training from the day your puppy arrives home, typically at 8 weeks. The 8–16 week window is the most sensitive socialisation period. Enrol in a puppy class within the first two weeks for structured socialisation alongside basic obedience foundations.

faqs.q: How long does it take to train a Broholmer?
faqs.a: Most Broholmers learn basic obedience cues (sit, stay, come, down) within 2–4 weeks of daily practice. Reliable recall in distracting environments typically takes 2–3 months of consistent reinforcement.

faqs.q: What health problems do Broholmers commonly have?
faqs.a: Broholmers are most commonly associated with routine age-related conditions. Regular vet checks, appropriate weight management, and breed-specific screening tests help detect issues early. Ask any breeder for health test results before purchasing.

faqs.q: How long do Broholmers live?
faqs.a: Broholmers have an average lifespan of 8–10 years. Larger breeds typically have shorter lifespans than smaller breeds. Maintaining a healthy weight and regular vet care are the most impactful factors for longevity.

faqs.q: Are Broholmers prone to hip dysplasia?
faqs.a: Broholmers have a moderate-to-elevated risk of hip dysplasia, particularly for large or active breeds. Ask for OFA or PennHIP hip evaluation certificates when buying from a breeder. Weight control and avoiding high-impact exercise during bone growth (under 18 months) reduces risk.

faqs.q: What health tests should a Broholmer puppy have?
faqs.a: At minimum, your Broholmer puppy should have a vet health check, first vaccinations, deworming, and microchipping before coming home. Ask the breeder for parent health certificates relevant to Broholmer-specific conditions. A vet check within 72 hours of bringing your puppy home is recommended to establish a baseline.

faqs.q: Are Broholmers good with kids?
faqs.a: Broholmers are generally known for being friendly and patient, making them well-suited to family life with children. Supervision is always recommended with young children regardless of breed — interactions should be taught from both sides.

faqs.q: Do Broholmers get along with other dogs?
faqs.a: Broholmers can be selective with other dogs due to their protective nature. Early socialisation in puppy classes and controlled on-lead introductions with other dogs help build positive associations.

faqs.q: Do Broholmers bark a lot?
faqs.a: Broholmers tend to be vocal — they may bark at strangers, sounds, or when under-stimulated. Adequate daily exercise and mental enrichment (training sessions, puzzle feeders) significantly reduce nuisance barking. Teaching a "quiet" cue early is worthwhile.

faqs.q: Are Broholmers good apartment dogs?
faqs.a: Broholmers adapt reasonably well to apartment living, particularly if they receive consistent daily walks and indoor enrichment. Their calm nature makes them less disruptive in confined spaces than high-energy large breeds.

faqs.q: How much exercise does a Broholmer need per day?
faqs.a: Broholmers need approximately 30–45 minutes of exercise daily. A structured morning walk and an evening sniff walk usually cover their needs. Mental exercise (training sessions, puzzle feeders) counts toward overall stimulation needs and can reduce restless behaviour.

faqs.q: Are Broholmers good running partners?
faqs.a: Broholmers are lower-energy dogs and are better suited to brisk walks or short jogs than distance running. Long runs can cause joint strain in lower-activity breeds — stick to 20–30 minute jogs rather than endurance runs.

faqs.q: What happens if a Broholmer doesn't get enough exercise?
faqs.a: Broholmers are less demanding than high-energy breeds, but chronic under-exercise still leads to weight gain and low-level restlessness. Even lower-energy breeds benefit from a consistent daily walk for both physical health and mental stimulation.

faqs.q: Can a Broholmer be off-lead?
faqs.a: Broholmers can be off-lead in secure areas once recall is reliable. Reliable recall typically takes 3–4 months of consistent training with progressive distance and distractions. Never trust off-lead recall in an unfenced area until it's been tested in controlled conditions first.

faqs.q: How much should I feed my Broholmer?
faqs.a: A Broholmer needs approximately 3–5 cups of dry food per day for an adult, split across two meals. Always follow the feeding guide on your specific formula — calorie density varies significantly between brands. Adjust portions based on body condition: you should be able to feel (but not easily see) the ribs.

faqs.q: How many times a day should I feed a Broholmer?
faqs.a: Adult Broholmers should eat twice daily. Puppies (under 6 months) need 3–4 smaller meals per day to support growth and prevent hypoglycaemia, particularly in small breeds. For large and giant breeds, twice daily feeding also reduces the risk of bloat (GDV) compared to one large daily meal.

faqs.q: What is the best food for a Broholmer?
faqs.a: Look for a formula carrying an AAFCO adequacy statement for the correct life stage. A named protein source (chicken, turkey, beef, salmon) should appear first in the ingredient list. Lower-energy Broholmers are prone to weight gain — choose a formula with controlled fat content and avoid calorie-dense performance formulas.

faqs.q: When should I switch my Broholmer from puppy to adult food?
faqs.a: Large breeds should stay on a large-breed puppy formula until 18–24 months, then transition to an adult formula. Switching too early can disrupt joint development during the growth phase.

faqs.q: Is a Broholmer a good dog for first-time owners?
faqs.a: Broholmers are manageable for motivated first-time owners who research the breed, commit to early training, and have realistic expectations about time and cost.

faqs.q: Are Broholmers good family dogs?
faqs.a: Broholmers are typically affectionate family dogs that do well with children and adapt to household routines. Their sociable nature means they prefer company over isolation.

faqs.q: Do Broholmers do well when left alone?
faqs.a: Broholmers form strong bonds with their owners and do not do well with extended isolation. Aim for no more than 4–6 hours alone at a time. If your schedule requires longer absences, consider a dog walker, doggy daycare, or a companion dog.

faqs.q: How much time do you need for a Broholmer?
faqs.a: Plan for 1–1.5 hours per day dedicated to your Broholmer — covering exercise, training, feeding and general interaction.  The commitment is consistent year-round, not just when convenient.
